prompt: You are a senior equity research associate at a bulge-bracket investment bank covering the Consumer Staples sector. Your managing director has asked you to prepare a quarterly variance analysis memo for Procter & Gamble Co (PG) based on the company's recently filed 10-Q for the fiscal third quarter ended March 31, 2026. The attached document contains key financial data extracted from the filing, including revenues, cost of goods sold, operating income, net income, diluted EPS, and SG&A expenses for Q1, Q2, and Q3 of fiscal 2026hol. Your task is to produce a professional memo (Word document format) addressed to the MD, analyzing PG's Q3 2026 performance versus the prior quarter (Q2 2026) and versus the same quarter last year (Q3 2025). The memo should include a cover page with the subject line 'PG Q3 FY2026 Variance Analysis', a header with standard memo fields (To, From, Date, Re), and the following sections: (1) Executive Summary – a brief overview of the quarter's key financial highlights; (2) Revenue Analysis – break down the sequential and year-over-year revenue changes, noting the absolute dollar and percentage variances; (3) Profitability Analysis – analyze operating income, net income, and diluted EPS, including margin trends; (4) Cost & Expense Review – discuss COGS, SG&A, and any notable expense line items; (5) Balance Sheet Summary – comment on total assets, liabilities, and cash position; and (6) Key Risks & Outlook – highlight any risks or trends evident from the filing data. Use a professional, concise writing style. All numbers must be drawn exclusively from the attached data. Do not include any external research or forecasts. The final deliverable should be a single .docx file.

paragraphs: This memo presents a variance analysis of Procter & Gamble Co's fiscal third quarter 2026 results, comparing them to the prior quarter (Q2 2026) and, where applicable, to the year-ago period (Q3 2025). All figures are sourced from the company's recent 10-Q filing.

For Q3 2026, PG reported total revenues of $21,235 million, a decrease of $973 million or approximately 4.4% from Q2 2026 revenues of $22,208 million. Operating income declined to $4,576 million from $5,366 million in the prior quarter, a drop of $790 million or 14.7%. Net income decreased to $3,932 million from $4,319 million, down $387 million or 9.0%. Diluted earnings per share fell to $1.63 from $1.78 in Q2 2026. These sequential declines reflect typical seasonal patterns and cost pressures discussed in the sections below.

paragraphs: PG's Q3 2026 revenue totaled $21,235 million, a decrease of $973 million from $22,208 million in Q2 2026, representing a sequential decline of 4.4%. Compared to Q1 2026 revenue of $22,386 million, Q3 revenue is $1,151 million lower, indicating a softening trend through the fiscal year. The provided data does not include Q3 2025 revenue, so a year-over-year comparison cannot be performed. The sequential decline may be attributable to seasonal demand patterns in consumer staples, particularly in the March quarter following the holiday-driven Q2 period.

paragraphs: Operating income for Q3 2026 was $4,576 million, down $790 million or 14.7% from $5,366 million in Q2 2026. The operating margin contracted to approximately 21.5% from 24.2% in the prior quarter, reflecting a larger proportional decline in operating income relative to revenue. Net income decreased to $3,932 million from $4,319 million, a drop of $387 million or 9.0%, resulting in a net margin of 18.5% versus 19.4% in Q2. Diluted EPS fell to $1.63 from $1.78, an 8.4% decline. For context, Q1 2026 operating income was $5,856 million and net income was $4,750 million, making Q3 the weakest quarter of the fiscal year to date on both metrics.

paragraphs: Cost of goods sold (COGS) in Q3 2026 was $10,722 million, down $112 million or 1.0% from $10,834 million in Q2 2026. However, as a percentage of revenue, COGS increased to 50.5% from 48.8%, indicating that the decline in COGS did not keep pace with the revenue decline. Selling, general and administrative (SG&A) expenses were $5,936 million in Q3, compared to $6,008 million in Q2, a decrease of $72 million or 1.2%. As a percentage of revenue, SG&A rose to 27.9% from 27.0%. The combined effect of these expense ratios drove the operating margin compression noted earlier. Research and development expense data is only available on an annual basis: $2,100 million in FY2025, $2,000 million in FY2024, and $2,000 million in FY2023.
